thread:
Alex Chen: Heads up — we're planning a short oncall evacuation test tomorrow 03:00 UTC (30m window). Intention: exercise pager bridge, run evacuation steps on a canary rack, and validate customer comms paths. Minimal customer impact expected but we want status page + support template ready.

Maya Patel: ack. what's the exact timeline? do we have a canary rack id? :thumbsup:

Alex Chen: timeline: 03:00 start, 03:05 begin controlled drain of canary serving nodes, 03:15 re-add nodes, 03:25 verify KV cache warm + traffic routing, 03:30 done. Canary rack: canary-eu1-03.

Oncall Bot: @channel Incident dry-run scheduled by Alex Chen at 2925554321 — pager will be sent to oncall rotation 03:00 UTC. Use #eng-oncall for comms; create bridge if escalation needed.

Mike Rivera: I'll own the runbook during the window. Will keep an eye on latency SLOs. I can open the bridge (zoom link below) if we need quick sync.

Alex Chen: bridge link: https://zoom.example/evac-test-2925554321 (use passcode: redwood). Mike — can you also post the statuspage draft?

Mike Rivera: sure. Draft status page (internal copy):
```
Status: Informational
Start: 03:00 UTC
Impact: None expected — routine oncall evacuation test on canary nodes. Some customers may see transient routing to fallback capacity for ~<1m while we verify KV cache.
What we're doing: Controlled drain and re-add of canary nodes to validate routing/fallback and oncall procedures.
Next update: 03:10 UTC
```

Emily Zhao: Customer-facing blurb (short):
"We are performing a brief operational test to validate our oncall evacuation procedures and routing fallbacks. Customers should see no interruption; in case of transient requests falling back to alternate capacity, requests will continue to be served. We do not expect any data loss."

Jordan (Support): I'll prep a support internal-facing template for CS with TL;DR and escalation steps. Customer L1s should use the canned response if they see inbound tickets.

Jordan (Support): Support template:
Hi <customer>,
We wanted to let you know we will be running a brief operational test at 03:00 UTC to validate our oncall evacuation flow. You should not experience any interruption. If you do notice increased latency or errors, please reply and include the request IDs and approximate times. Our oncall team will respond as priority.

Alex Chen: Good. Also need internal ops checklist to attach to the status page update. Mike, can you paste the checklist items you'll run?

Mike Rivera: checklist snippet:
- Confirm canary rack health before drain (`/infra/racks/canary-eu1-03 status`)
- Start drain: `evacuate --rack canary-eu1-03 --mode controlled --grace 30s`
- Watch M-Latency /p99 and request failures dashboard (link)
- If failures > threshold: abort and re-add nodes, escalate to eng-sre
- Warm KV cache: run `kv-warm --targets 3 --prefix common`
- Verify routing metrics stable for 5m before closing

Oncall Bot: Pager sent to rotation: oncall-primary at 03:00 UTC. Reaction: :rotating_light: if any alert triggers during window.

Maya Patel: small nit — can we add a short line about customers on dedicated/private? some Dedicated customers will be isolated; mention that in the page.

Alex Chen: good call. Revised customer blurb with dedicated note:
"We are performing a brief operational test to validate our oncall evacuation flow. Most customers will see no interruption; a small subset of Dedicated customers may be on isolated capacity and will not be affected by this canary test. In case of transient requests falling back to alternate capacity, requests will continue to be served. We do not expect any data loss."

Mike Rivera: I'm going to post the status page update at 03:02 UTC (internal first), and then push to public statuspage at 03:05 after initial drain starts. Who's on content sign-off? Jordan? Maya?

Jordan (Support): I'll review CS copy and sign-off by 02:45 UTC.

Maya Patel: I'll review the public blurb and ops checklist by 02:50 UTC.

Deploy Bot: Auto-check: canary-eu1-03 last deployment was 2026-02-28T22:12Z — no open rollouts.

Alex Chen: cool. Quick escalation plan in case the canary drain causes >1% error rate sustained for 2 minutes:
- Step 1: abort/dryrun reverse (`evacuate --rack canary-eu1-03 --mode abort`)
- Step 2: move traffic back to primary pool and open emergency bridge with eng-sre
- Step 3: prepare customer statement: "We observed elevated error rates during a routine test; we reversed the change and are investigating. No data loss. Full RCA will follow."

Maya Patel: noted. also filing a post-test checklist item: capture traces for 10m after re-add to help regression detection.

Oncall Bot: 02:58 UTC reminder: pager will fire in 2 minutes for oncall rotation.

Alex Chen: final ask — after we close, can someone post a short completion notice here and update status page to "All clear — testing complete"? I'll file a follow-up RCA stub.

Mike Rivera: will post completion and metrics at ~03:35 UTC with p95/p99 and error delta.

Jordan (Support): I'll send an internal note to CS with the final outcome and any templated replies used.

Oncall Bot: 03:35 UTC — Test completed; no customer-impacting incidents detected.

Alex Chen: thanks all. I'll file the RCA stub and link to the logs. Great run. :tada:
